# treemd

A markdown navigator with tree-based structural navigation. Navigate markdown documents using an expandable/collapsible heading tree with a synchronized content view.

![treemd screenshot showing dual-pane interface](assets/output.gif)

## Overview

treemd is a modern markdown viewer that combines the structural clarity of a tree-style outline with powerful interactive navigation. Use it to:

- Navigate large documents by collapsing/expanding heading sections
- Search headings or full document content with highlighted matches
- Edit tables, toggle checkboxes, and follow links without leaving the terminal
- Extract specific sections or query markdown elements with a jq-like syntax
- Pipe markdown from stdin for shell-scripted workflows

## Features

- Dual-pane interface: outline + synchronized content view
- Interactive mode: navigate, edit, and interact with tables, checkboxes, links, and code blocks
- Table editing and navigation
- Checkbox toggling with optional file updates
- Link following (anchors, files, URLs)
- Search and filter headings or content
- Multiple color themes and customizable keybindings
- CLI mode for scripting and extraction

## Installation

Install using common package managers if available for your platform.

Homebrew (macOS / Linux):

```bash
brew install treemd
```

Arch Linux (pacman):

```bash
pacman -S treemd
```

On systems that provide pre-built packages, prefer the packaged binaries for your platform.

## Usage

### TUI Mode (Interactive)

Launch the interactive interface by running treemd with a file or directory:

```bash
treemd README.md        # Open specific file
treemd .                # Open file picker in current directory
treemd docs/            # Open file picker in specified directory
treemd *.md             # Open file picker with matched files
```

Common navigation keys (typical): j/k, g/G, Enter/Space to expand/collapse, Tab to switch focus, q to quit.

### CLI Mode (Non-Interactive)

List headings:

```bash
treemd -l README.md
```

Show heading tree:

```bash
treemd --tree README.md
```

Extract a section:

```bash
treemd -s "Installation" README.md
```

Filter and level options:

```bash
treemd -l --filter "usage" README.md    # Filter by text
treemd -l -L 2 README.md                # Only ## headings
```

Count and JSON output:

```bash
treemd --count README.md                # Count by level
treemd -l -o json README.md             # JSON output
```

## Query Language

treemd includes a jq-like query language for extracting markdown elements. Use -q to execute queries.

Examples:

```bash
treemd -q '.h' doc.md         # All headings
treemd -q '.h2' doc.md        # Level 2 headings
treemd -q '.code' doc.md      # Code blocks
treemd -q '.link' doc.md      # Links
```

Pipes and functions:

```bash
treemd -q '.h2 | text' doc.md
treemd -q '[.h] | count' doc.md
```

## Configuration

User configuration is stored in a platform-appropriate config file (e.g. under ~/.config/treemd/ on Unix-like systems). Themes and keybindings are customizable via that config.

treemd Query Language (tql)

A jq-like query language for navigating and extracting markdown structure.

ELEMENT SELECTORS
    .h, .heading    All headings (any level)
    .h1 - .h6       Headings by level
    .code           All code blocks
    .code[rust]     Code blocks by language
    .link, .a       All links
    .link[external] External links only
    .img            All images
    .table          All tables
    .list           All lists
    .blockquote     All blockquotes

FILTERS & INDEXING
    .h2[Features]       Heading containing "Features" (fuzzy)
    .h2["Installation"] Heading with exact text
    .h2[0]              First h2
    .h2[-1]             Last h2
    .h2[1:3]            h2s at index 1 and 2
    .h2[:3]             First 3 h2s

HIERARCHY
    .h1 > .h2           Direct child h2s under h1s
    .h1 >> .code        Code blocks anywhere under h1s

PIPES
    .h2 | text          Get heading text (strips ##)
    [.h2] | count       Count all h2s
    .code | lang        Get code block languages
    .link | url         Get link URLs

COLLECTION FUNCTIONS
    count, length       Count elements (alias: len, size)
    first, last         First/last element (alias: head)
    limit(n), take(n)   First n elements
    skip(n), drop(n)    Skip first n elements
    nth(n)              Get element at index
    reverse             Reverse order
    sort                Sort alphabetically
    sort_by(key)        Sort by property
    unique              Remove duplicates
    flatten             Flatten nested arrays
    group_by(key)       Group elements by key
    min, max            Min/max numeric value
    add                 Sum numbers or concat strings

STRING FUNCTIONS
    text                Get text representation
    upper, lower        Case conversion
    trim                Strip whitespace
    split(sep)          Split by separator
    join(sep)           Join with separator
    replace(a, b)       Replace substring
    slugify             URL-friendly slug
    lines, words, chars Count lines/words/chars

FILTER FUNCTIONS
    select(cond)        Keep if condition true (alias: where, filter)
    contains(s)         Contains substring (alias: includes)
    startswith(s)       Starts with prefix
    endswith(s)         Ends with suffix
    matches(regex)      Matches regex pattern
    any, all            Check if any/all truthy
    not                 Negate boolean

CONTENT FUNCTIONS
    content             Section content (for headings)
    md                  Raw markdown
    url, href, src      Get URL/link/image source
    lang                Code block language

AGGREGATION FUNCTIONS
    stats               Document statistics
    levels              Heading count by level
    langs               Code block count by language
    types               Link types count

EXAMPLES
    # List all h2 headings
    treemd -q '.h2' doc.md

    # Get heading text only
    treemd -q '.h2 | text' doc.md

    # Count headings
    treemd -q '[.h2] | count' doc.md

    # First 5 headings
    treemd -q '[.h] | limit(5)' doc.md

    # Filter headings (three equivalent ways)
    treemd -q '.h | select(contains("API"))' doc.md
    treemd -q '.h | where(contains("API"))' doc.md
    treemd -q '.h[API]' doc.md

    # All Rust code blocks
    treemd -q '.code[rust]' doc.md

    # External link URLs
    treemd -q '.link[external] | url' doc.md

    # h2s under "Features" section
    treemd -q '.h1[Features] > .h2' doc.md

    # Group headings by level
    treemd -q '[.h] | group_by("level")' doc.md

    # Document statistics
    treemd -q '. | stats' doc.md

    # JSON output
    treemd -q '.h2' --query-output json doc.md

OUTPUT FORMATS (--query-output)
    plain       Human-readable text (default)
    json        Compact JSON
    json-pretty Pretty-printed JSON (alias: jsonp)
    jsonl       Line-delimited JSON (one per line)
    md          Raw markdown
    tree        Tree structure

# treemd

A markdown navigator with tree-based structural navigation. Navigate markdown documents using an expandable/collapsible heading tree with a synchronized content view.

![treemd screenshot showing dual-pane interface](assets/output.gif)

## Overview

treemd is a modern markdown viewer that combines the structural clarity of a tree-style outline with powerful interactive navigation. Use it to:

- Navigate large documents by collapsing/expanding heading sections
- Search headings or full document content with highlighted matches
- Edit tables, toggle checkboxes, and follow links without leaving the terminal
- Extract specific sections or query markdown elements with a jq-like syntax
- Pipe markdown from stdin for shell-scripted workflows

## Features

- Dual-pane interface: outline + synchronized content view
- Interactive mode: navigate, edit, and interact with tables, checkboxes, links, and code blocks
- Table editing and navigation
- Checkbox toggling with optional file updates
- Link following (anchors, files, URLs)
- Search and filter headings or content
- Multiple color themes and customizable keybindings
- CLI mode for scripting and extraction

## Installation

Install using common package managers if available for your platform.

Homebrew (macOS / Linux):

```bash
brew install treemd
```

Arch Linux (pacman):

```bash
pacman -S treemd
```

On systems that provide pre-built packages, prefer the packaged binaries for your platform.

## Usage

### TUI Mode (Interactive)

Launch the interactive interface by running treemd with a file or directory:

```bash
treemd README.md        # Open specific file
treemd .                # Open file picker in current directory
treemd docs/            # Open file picker in specified directory
treemd *.md             # Open file picker with matched files
```

Common navigation keys (typical): j/k, g/G, Enter/Space to expand/collapse, Tab to switch focus, q to quit.

### CLI Mode (Non-Interactive)

List headings:

```bash
treemd -l README.md
```

Show heading tree:

```bash
treemd --tree README.md
```

Extract a section:

```bash
treemd -s "Installation" README.md
```

Filter and level options:

```bash
treemd -l --filter "usage" README.md    # Filter by text
treemd -l -L 2 README.md                # Only ## headings
```

Count and JSON output:

```bash
treemd --count README.md                # Count by level
treemd -l -o json README.md             # JSON output
```

## Query Language

treemd includes a jq-like query language for extracting markdown elements. Use -q to execute queries.

Examples:

# Title
## Section One
### Subsection 1.1
## Section Two
### Subsection 2.1
#### Subsub 2.1.1
## Installation
---
└──# Title
   ├──## Section One
   │  └──### Subsection 1.1
   ├──## Section Two
   │  └──### Subsection 2.1
   │     └──#### Subsub 2.1.1
   └──## Installation
---
Heading counts:
  #: 1
  ##: 3
  ###: 2
  ####: 1

Total: 7

# treemd

A markdown navigator with tree-based structural navigation. Navigate markdown documents using an expandable/collapsible heading tree with a synchronized content view.

![treemd screenshot showing dual-pane interface](assets/output.gif)

## Overview

treemd is a modern markdown viewer that combines the structural clarity of a tree-style outline with powerful interactive navigation. Use it to:

- Navigate large documents by collapsing/expanding heading sections
- Search headings or full document content with highlighted matches
- Edit tables, toggle checkboxes, and follow links without leaving the terminal
- Extract specific sections or query markdown elements with a jq-like syntax
- Pipe markdown from stdin for shell-scripted workflows

## Features

- Dual-pane interface: outline + synchronized content view
- Interactive mode: navigate, edit, and interact with tables, checkboxes, links, and code blocks
- Table editing and navigation
- Checkbox toggling with optional file updates
- Link following (anchors, files, URLs)
- Search and filter headings or content
- Multiple color themes and customizable keybindings
- CLI mode for scripting and extraction

## Installation

Install using common package managers if available for your platform.

function _clap_dynamic_completer_treemd() {
    local _CLAP_COMPLETE_INDEX=$(expr $CURRENT - 1)
    local _CLAP_IFS=$'\n'

    local completions=("${(@f)$( \
        _CLAP_IFS="$_CLAP_IFS" \
        _CLAP_COMPLETE_INDEX="$_CLAP_COMPLETE_INDEX" \
        COMPLETE="zsh" \
        /workspace/./executable -- "${words[@]}" 2>/dev/null \
    )}")

    if [[ -n $completions ]]; then
        local -a dirs=()
        local -a other=()
        local completion
        for completion in $completions; do
            local value="${completion%%:*}"
            if [[ "$value" == */ ]]; then
                local dir_no_slash="${value%/}"
                if [[ "$completion" == *:* ]]; then
                    local desc="${completion#*:}"
                    dirs+=("$dir_no_slash:$desc")
                else
                    dirs+=("$dir_no_slash")
                fi
            else
                other+=("$completion")
            fi
        done
        [[ -n $dirs ]] && _describe 'values' dirs -S '/' -r '/'
        [[ -n $other ]] && _describe 'values' other
    fi
}

function _clap_dynamic_completer_treemd() {
    local _CLAP_COMPLETE_INDEX=$(expr $CURRENT - 1)
    local _CLAP_IFS=$'\n'

    local completions=("${(@f)$( \
        _CLAP_IFS="$_CLAP_IFS" \

        COMPLETE="zsh" \

    if [[ -n $completions ]]; then
        local -a dirs=()
        local -a other=()
        local completion
        for completion in $completions; do
            local value="${completion%%:*}"
            if [[ "$value" == */ ]]; then
                local dir_no_slash="${value%/}"
                if [[ "$completion" == *:* ]]; then
                    local desc="${completion#*:}"
                    dirs+=("$dir_no_slash:$desc")
                else
                    dirs+=("$dir_no_slash")
                fi
            else
                other+=("$completion")
            fi
        done
        [[ -n $dirs ]] && _describe 'values' dirs -S '/' -r '/'
        [[ -n $other ]] && _describe 'values' other
    fi

A jq-like query language for navigating and extracting markdown structure.

    .h1 >> .code        Code blocks anywhere under h1s

treemd Query Language (tql)

A jq-like query language for navigating and extracting markdown structure.

ELEMENT SELECTORS
    .h, .heading    All headings (any level)
    .h1 - .h6       Headings by level
    .code           All code blocks
    .code[rust]     Code blocks by language

    .img            All images
    .table          All tables
    .list           All lists
    .blockquote     All blockquotes

    .h2[0]              First h2
    .h2[-1]             Last h2
    .h2[1:3]            h2s at index 1 and 2
    .h2[:3]             First 3 h2s

    .h1 > .h2           Direct child h2s under h1s
    .h1 >> .code        Code blocks anywhere under h1s

    [.h2] | count       Count all h2s

    .link | url         Get link URLs

    sort_by(key)        Sort by property
    unique              Remove duplicates

    group_by(key)       Group elements by key

    add                 Sum numbers or concat strings

    endswith(s)         Ends with suffix

import re

def parse_markdown(content):
    """
    Returns list of headings with fields: level, title, line_num (1-indexed heading line), offset (cumulative offset of next line start), heading_line_start_offset
    """
    lines = content.splitlines(keepends=True)
    # To compute offsets, need cumulative
    headings=[]
    offset=0
    for idx, line in enumerate(lines):
        line_num=idx+1
        # Check for heading: optional leading spaces (spaces only? not tab), then 1-6 #, then space
        # According spec, heading requires # at start after optional spaces (0-3 spaces allowed in markdown? but we saw 3 spaces works)
        # We'll allow up to 3 leading spaces? Test showed 3 spaces works. Let's allow any number of spaces (not tab) for simplicity, but tab fails.
        # Our earlier test: "   # Title" (3 spaces) worked, " # Title" (1 space) worked, tab failed.
        m=re.match(r'^[ ]{0,3}(#{1,6})[ \t]+(.*)$', line)
        if m:
            hashes=m.group(1)
            level=len(hashes)
            title_raw=m.group(2)
            # Title trimmed and also need to remove trailing spaces and maybe trailing #'s? Not needed per tests, but we trim
            title=title_raw.strip()
            # For display, remove trailing hash? Not needed

                'line_num': line_num,
                'heading_offset': offset,
                'next_offset': next_offset, # start of next line
                'position_line': line_num+1,
                'position_offset': next_offset,

        offset+=len(line)

                    res.append({'type': 'strong', 'value': m.group(2)})
                elif m.group(3) is not None: # image alt, src
                    alt=m.group(3)
                    src_full=m.group(4)
                    # src may contain title in quotes? simplified
                    src=src_full.split()[0]
                    title=None
                    # check for title
                    if '"' in src_full or "'" in src_full:

                        # naive
                        t_match=re.search(r'["\'](.+)["\']', src_full)
                        if t_match:
                            title=t_match.group(1)
                    res.append({'type': 'image', 'alt': alt, 'src': src, 'title': title})
                elif m.group(5) is not None: # link
                    text=m.group(5)
                    url_full=m.group(6)
                    url=url_full.split()[0]
                    title=None
                    # check title
                    t_match=re.search(r'["\'](.+)["\']', url_full)
                    if t_match:

                    res.append({'type': 'link', 'text': text, 'url': url, 'title': title})
                pos=end
            if pos < len(s):
                res.append({'type': 'text', 'value': s[pos:]})
            # If no matches, ensure at least one text
            if not res:
                res.append({'type': 'text', 'value': s})
            return res

        inlines=parse_inline(para_text)
        blocks.append({
            'type': 'paragraph',
            'content': para_text,
            'inline': inlines
        })
    return blocks

Launch without flags for interactive mode with dual-pane interface, vim-style navigation,

Examples:

Options:
  -l, --list

      --tree

      --filter <PATTERN>

A jq-like query language for navigating and extracting markdown structure.

"""

ATLINE_HELP_LONG="""Show heading at specific line number

Finds and displays the heading that appears at or before the given line number. Useful for jumping to a specific location in the document structure.

Usage: {prog} at-line <LINE>

Arguments:
  <LINE>
          Line number in the markdown file
          
          The line number to search for. Returns the heading at or immediately before this line.

Options:
  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')
"""

ATLINE_HELP_SHORT="""Show heading at specific line number

Usage: {prog} at-line <LINE>

Arguments:
  <LINE>  Line number in the markdown file

Options:
  -h, --help  Print help (see more with '--help')
"""

def slugify(text):
    s=text.lower().strip()
    filtered=""
    for ch in s:
        if ch.isalnum() or ch in [" ", "-"]:
            filtered+=ch
    filtered=filtered.replace(" ", "-")
    filtered=re.sub(r"-+", "-", filtered)
    filtered=filtered.strip("-")
    return filtered

def parse_headings(content):
    lines = content.splitlines(keepends=True)
    headings=[]
    offset=0
    for idx,line in enumerate(lines):
        # limit leading spaces to 3, spaces only (not tab)
        # match pattern: up to 3 spaces, then 1-6 #, then space/tab, then title
        m=re.match(r'^[ ]{0,3}(#{1,6})[ \t]+(.*)$', line)
        if m:
            level=len(m.group(1))
            title=m.group(2).strip()
            # For some cases, title may include trailing #? Keep as is stripped.
            next_offset=offset+len(line)
            headings.append({
                'level': level,
                'title': title,
                'line_num': idx+1,
                'heading_offset': offset,
                'next_offset': next_offset,
                'position_line': idx+2,
                'position_offset': next_offset,
            })
        offset+=len(line)
    return headings, lines

def build_tree(headings):
    nodes=[]
    stack=[]
    for h in headings:
        node={
            'level': h['level'],
            'title': h['title'],
            'slug': slugify(h['title']),
            'id': slugify(h['title']),
            'position': {'line': h['position_line'], 'offset': h['position_offset']},
            'line_num': h['line_num'],
            'heading_offset': h['heading_offset'],
            'next_offset': h['next_offset'],
            'children': [],
            'content_raw': '',
        }
        while stack and stack[-1]['level'] >= node['level']:
            stack.pop()
        if stack:
            stack[-1]['children'].append(node)
        else:
            nodes.append(node)
        stack.append(node)
    return nodes

def compute_content(nodes, content, headings):
    flat=[]
    def flatten(ns):
        for n in ns:
            flat.append(n)
            flatten(n['children'])
    flatten(nodes)
    for i in range(len(headings)):
        if i >= len(flat):
            break
        node=flat[i]
        next_off = headings[i+1]['heading_offset'] if i+1 < len(headings) else len(content)
        start = node['position']['offset']
        raw_slice = content[start:next_off]
        node['content_raw'] = raw_slice.strip()
    return nodes

def parse_document(content, synthetic=None):
    # synthetic: None or "input" or "select"
    # Returns nodes, headings, content, metadata
    if synthetic == "select":
        # single heading Select a file
        title="Select a file"
        slug=slugify(title)
        node={
            'level': 1,
            'title': title,
            'slug': slug,
            'id': slug,
            'position': {'line': 2, 'offset': 16},
            'line_num': 1,
            'heading_offset': 0,
            'next_offset': 16,
            'children': [],
            'content_raw': "Press Enter to select a markdown file.",
        }
        headings=[{'level':1,'title':title,'line_num':1,'heading_offset':0,'next_offset':16,'position_line':2,'position_offset':16}]
        metadata={'source': None, 'headingCount':1, 'maxDepth':1, 'wordCount': 11}
        return [node], headings, "# Select a file\n\nPress Enter to select a markdown file.\n", metadata
    if synthetic == "input":
        # Input synthetic with content = original content trimmed? But we need to keep original for word count?
        # For metadata wordCount we compute based on synthetic doc: "# Input\n\n"+content
        # But for simplicity, if content empty, raw empty
        # Node content_raw = content stripped
        title="Input"
        slug=slugify(title)
        node={
            'level': 1,
            'title': title,
            'slug': slug,
            'id': slug,
            'position': {'line': 2, 'offset': 8},
            'line_num': 1,
            'heading_offset': 0,
            'next_offset': 8,
            'children': [],
            'content_raw': content.strip(),
        }
        headings=[{'level':1,'title':title,'line_num':1,'heading_offset':0,'next_offset':8,'position_line':2,'position_offset':8}]
        # word count = tokens of synthetic
        synthetic_text = f"# Input\n\n{content}"
        wc = len(synthetic_text.split()) if synthetic_text.strip() else 2
        # Actually for empty content, wc should be 2
        if not content.strip():
            wc=2
        metadata={'source': None, 'headingCount':1, 'maxDepth':1, 'wordCount': wc}
        return [node], headings, synthetic_text, metadata

    headings, lines = parse_headings(content)
    if not headings:
        # No headings -> Input synthetic
        return parse_document(content, synthetic="input")
    nodes=build_tree(headings)
    nodes=compute_content(nodes, content, headings)
    # metadata
    max_depth=max(h['level'] for h in headings) if headings else 1
    wc=len(content.split())
    metadata={'source': None, 'headingCount': len(headings), 'maxDepth': max_depth, 'wordCount': wc}
    return nodes, headings, content, metadata

def flatten_nodes(nodes):
    flat=[]
    def rec(ns):
        for n in ns:
            flat.append(n)
            rec(n['children'])
    rec(nodes)
    return flat

def render_list_plain(nodes, filter_pat=None, level=None):

def render_tree_box(nodes):
    lines=[]
    def recurse(ns, prefix_parts):
        for idx, node in enumerate(ns):
            is_last = (idx == len(ns)-1)
            prefix=""
            for is_last_anc in prefix_parts:
                prefix += "   " if is_last_anc else "│  "
            connector="└──" if is_last else "├──"
            heading_text=f"{'#'*node['level']} {node['title']}"
            lines.append(f"{prefix}{connector}{heading_text}")
            recurse(node['children'], prefix_parts+[is_last])
    recurse(nodes, [])
    return "\n".join(lines)

def parse_blocks(text):
    # Very similar to earlier implementation
    lines=text.splitlines()
    blocks=[]
    i=0
    while i < len(lines):
        line=lines[i]
        if not line.strip():
            i+=1
            continue
        # code fence
        stripped=line.strip()
        if stripped.startswith("```"):
            lang=stripped[3:].strip() or None
            j=i+1
            content_lines=[]
            while j < len(lines) and not lines[j].strip().startswith("```"):
                content_lines.append(lines[j])
                j+=1
            content="\n".join(content_lines)
            blocks.append({
                'type': 'code',
                'language': lang,
                'content': content,
                'start_line': 2,
                'end_line': 2,
            })
            i=j+1
            continue
        # table
        if '|' in line and i+1 < len(lines) and re.match(r'^\s*\|?[\s\-\|:]+\|?[\s\-\|:]+\s*$', lines[i+1]) and '|' in lines[i+1]:
            def split_row(row):
                row=row.strip()
                if row.startswith('|'):
                    row=row[1:]
                if row.endswith('|'):
                    row=row[:-1]
                cols=[c.strip() for c in row.split('|')]
                return cols
            headers=split_row(line)
            i+=2
            rows=[]
            while i < len(lines) and '|' in lines[i] and lines[i].strip():
                rows.append(split_row(lines[i]))
                i+=1
            blocks.append({
                'type': 'table',
                'headers': headers,
                'alignments': ['none']*len(headers),
                'rows': rows,
            })
            continue
        # list
        m=re.match(r'^\s*([-*+]\s+|\d+\.\s+)', line)
        if m:
            items=[]
            ordered=bool(re.match(r'^\s*\d+\.\s+', line))
            while i < len(lines):
                if not lines[i].strip():
                    # check next
                    if i+1 < len(lines) and re.match(r'^\s*([-*+]\s+|\d+\.\s+)', lines[i+1]):
                        i+=1
                        continue
                    else:
                        break
                if not re.match(r'^\s*([-*+]\s+|\d+\.\s+)', lines[i]):
                    break
                l=lines[i]
                cb_match=re.match(r'^\s*[-*+]\s+\[([ xX])\]\s+(.*)', l)
                if cb_match:
                    checked=cb_match.group(1).lower()=='x'
                    content_text=cb_match.group(2).strip()
                    items.append({
                        'checked': checked,
                        'content': content_text,
                        'inline': [{'type': 'text', 'value': content_text}]
                    })
                else:
                    content_text=re.sub(r'^\s*([-*+]\s+|\d+\.\s+)', '', l).strip()
                    items.append({
                        'checked': None,
                        'content': content_text,
                        'inline': [{'type': 'text', 'value': content_text}]
                    })
                i+=1
            blocks.append({
                'type': 'list',
                'ordered': ordered,
                'items': items
            })
            continue
        # blockquote
        if line.lstrip().startswith('>'):
            bq_lines=[]
            while i < len(lines) and lines[i].lstrip().startswith('>'):
                bq_lines.append(re.sub(r'^\s*>\s?', '', lines[i]))
                i+=1
            content_text=" ".join(bq_lines).strip()
            blocks.append({
                'type': 'blockquote',
                'content': content_text,
                'blocks': [{
                    'type': 'paragraph',
                    'content': content_text,
                    'inline': [{'type': 'text', 'value': content_text}]
                }]
            })
            continue
        # paragraph
        para_lines=[]
        while i < len(lines) and lines[i].strip():
            # break if special
            if lines[i].strip().startswith("```"):
                break
            if '|' in lines[i] and i+1 < len(lines) and re.match(r'^\s*\|?[\s\-\|:]+\|?', lines[i+1]) and '|' in lines[i+1]:
                break
            if re.match(r'^\s*([-*+]\s+|\d+\.\s+)', lines[i]):
                break
            if lines[i].lstrip().startswith('>'):
                break
            para_lines.append(lines[i])
            i+=1
            if i < len(lines) and not lines[i].strip():
                break
        para_text=" ".join([l.strip() for l in para_lines])
        # inline parse
        def parse_inline(s):
            res=[]
            pattern=re.compile(r'(\*\*(.+?)\*\*|!\[([^\]]*)\]\(([^\)]+)\)|\[([^\]]+)\]\(([^\)]+)\))')
            pos=0
            for mm in pattern.finditer(s):
                start,end=mm.span()
                if start>pos:
                    res.append({'type':'text','value':s[pos:start]})
                if mm.group(2):
                    res.append({'type':'strong','value':mm.group(2)})
                elif mm.group(3) is not None:
                    alt=mm.group(3)
                    src_full=mm.group(4)
                    src=src_full.split()[0]
                    title=None
                    tm=re.search(r'["\'](.+)["\']', src_full)
                    if tm:
                        title=tm.group(1)
                    res.append({'type':'image','alt':alt,'src':src,'title':title})
                elif mm.group(5) is not None:
                    t=mm.group(5)
                    url_full=mm.group(6)
                    url=url_full.split()[0]
                    title=None
                    tm=re.search(r'["\'](.+)["\']', url_full)
                    if tm:
                        title=tm.group(1)
                    res.append({'type':'link','text':t,'url':url,'title':title})
                pos=end
            if pos < len(s):
                res.append({'type':'text','value':s[pos:]})
            if not res:
                res.append({'type':'text','value':s})
            return res
        inlines=parse_inline(para_text)
        blocks.append({
            'type':'paragraph',
            'content':para_text,
            'inline':inlines
        })
    return blocks

def slugify(text):
    s=text.lower().strip()
    filtered=""
    for ch in s:
        if ch.isalnum() or ch in [" ", "-"]:
            filtered+=ch
    filtered=filtered.replace(" ", "-")
    filtered=re.sub(r"-+", "-", filtered)
    filtered=filtered.strip("-")
    return filtered

def parse_headings(content):
    lines = content.splitlines(keepends=True)
    headings=[]
    offset=0
    for idx,line in enumerate(lines):
        # limit leading spaces to 3, spaces only (not tab)
        # match pattern: up to 3 spaces, then 1-6 #, then space/tab, then title
        m=re.match(r'^[ ]{0,3}(#{1,6})[ \t]+(.*)$', line)
        if m:
            level=len(m.group(1))
            title=m.group(2).strip()
            # For some cases, title may include trailing #? Keep as is stripped.
            next_offset=offset+len(line)
            headings.append({
                'level': level,
                'title': title,
                'line_num': idx+1,
                'heading_offset': offset,
                'next_offset': next_offset,
                'position_line': idx+2,
                'position_offset': next_offset,
            })
        offset+=len(line)
    return headings, lines

def build_tree(headings):
    nodes=[]
    stack=[]
    for h in headings:
        node={
            'level': h['level'],
            'title': h['title'],
            'slug': slugify(h['title']),
            'id': slugify(h['title']),
            'position': {'line': h['position_line'], 'offset': h['position_offset']},
            'line_num': h['line_num'],
            'heading_offset': h['heading_offset'],
            'next_offset': h['next_offset'],
            'children': [],
            'content_raw': '',
        }
        while stack and stack[-1]['level'] >= node['level']:
            stack.pop()
        if stack:
            stack[-1]['children'].append(node)
        else:
            nodes.append(node)
        stack.append(node)
    return nodes

def compute_content(nodes, content, headings):
    flat=[]
    def flatten(ns):
        for n in ns:
            flat.append(n)
            flatten(n['children'])
    flatten(nodes)
    for i in range(len(headings)):
        if i >= len(flat):
            break
        node=flat[i]
        next_off = headings[i+1]['heading_offset'] if i+1 < len(headings) else len(content)
        start = node['position']['offset']
        raw_slice = content[start:next_off]
        node['content_raw'] = raw_slice.strip()
    return nodes

def flatten_nodes(nodes):
    flat=[]
    def rec(ns):
        for n in ns:
            flat.append(n)
            rec(n['children'])
    rec(nodes)
    return flat

def render_list_plain(nodes, filter_pat=None, level=None):
    flat=flatten_nodes(nodes)
    # If both filter and level provided, only level applies (observed)
    if filter_pat is not None and level is not None:
        filter_pat=None
    if level is not None:
        flat=[h for h in flat if h['level']==level]
    elif filter_pat is not None:
        pat=filter_pat.lower()
        flat=[h for h in flat if pat in h['title'].lower()]

def render_tree_box(nodes):
    lines=[]
    def recurse(ns, prefix_parts):
        for idx, node in enumerate(ns):
            is_last = (idx == len(ns)-1)
            prefix=""
            for is_last_anc in prefix_parts:
                prefix += "   " if is_last_anc else "│  "
            connector="└──" if is_last else "├──"
            heading_text=f"{'#'*node['level']} {node['title']}"
            lines.append(f"{prefix}{connector}{heading_text}")
            recurse(node['children'], prefix_parts+[is_last])
    recurse(nodes, [])
    return "\n".join(lines)

def render_count(nodes):
    flat=flatten_nodes(nodes)
    # count by level
    counts={}
    for h in flat:
        counts[h['level']]=counts.get(h['level'],0)+1
    total=len(flat)
    out_lines=["Heading counts:"]
    for lvl in sorted(counts.keys()):
        out_lines.append(f"  {'#'*lvl}: {counts[lvl]}")
    out_lines.append("")
    out_lines.append(f"Total: {total}")
    return "\n".join(out_lines)

def parse_blocks(text):
    # Very similar to earlier implementation
    lines=text.splitlines()
    blocks=[]
    i=0
    while i < len(lines):
        line=lines[i]
        if not line.strip():
            i+=1
            continue
        # code fence
        stripped=line.strip()
        if stripped.startswith("```"):
            lang=stripped[3:].strip() or None
            j=i+1
            content_lines=[]
            while j < len(lines) and not lines[j].strip().startswith("```"):
                content_lines.append(lines[j])
                j+=1
            content="\n".join(content_lines)
            blocks.append({
                'type': 'code',
                'language': lang,
                'content': content,
                'start_line': 2,
                'end_line': 2,
            })
            i=j+1
            continue
        # table
        if '|' in line and i+1 < len(lines) and re.match(r'^\s*\|?[\s\-\|:]+\|?[\s\-\|:]+\s*$', lines[i+1]) and '|' in lines[i+1]:
            def split_row(row):
                row=row.strip()
                if row.startswith('|'):
                    row=row[1:]
                if row.endswith('|'):
                    row=row[:-1]
                cols=[c.strip() for c in row.split('|')]
                return cols
            headers=split_row(line)
            i+=2
            rows=[]
            while i < len(lines) and '|' in lines[i] and lines[i].strip():
                rows.append(split_row(lines[i]))
                i+=1
            blocks.append({
                'type': 'table',
                'headers': headers,
                'alignments': ['none']*len(headers),
                'rows': rows,
            })
            continue
        # list
        m=re.match(r'^\s*([-*+]\s+|\d+\.\s+)', line)
        if m:
            items=[]
            ordered=bool(re.match(r'^\s*\d+\.\s+', line))
            while i < len(lines):
                if not lines[i].strip():
                    # check next
                    if i+1 < len(lines) and re.match(r'^\s*([-*+]\s+|\d+\.\s+)', lines[i+1]):
                        i+=1
                        continue
                    else:
                        break
                if not re.match(r'^\s*([-*+]\s+|\d+\.\s+)', lines[i]):
                    break
                l=lines[i]
                cb_match=re.match(r'^\s*[-*+]\s+\[([ xX])\]\s+(.*)', l)
                if cb_match:
                    checked=cb_match.group(1).lower()=='x'
                    content_text=cb_match.group(2).strip()
                    items.append({
                        'checked': checked,
                        'content': content_text,
                        'inline': [{'type': 'text', 'value': content_text}]
                    })
                else:
                    content_text=re.sub(r'^\s*([-*+]\s+|\d+\.\s+)', '', l).strip()
                    items.append({
                        'checked': None,
                        'content': content_text,
                        'inline': [{'type': 'text', 'value': content_text}]
                    })
                i+=1
            blocks.append({
                'type': 'list',
                'ordered': ordered,
                'items': items
            })
            continue
        # blockquote
        if line.lstrip().startswith('>'):
            bq_lines=[]
            while i < len(lines) and lines[i].lstrip().startswith('>'):
                bq_lines.append(re.sub(r'^\s*>\s?', '', lines[i]))
                i+=1
            content_text=" ".join(bq_lines).strip()
            blocks.append({
                'type': 'blockquote',
                'content': content_text,
                'blocks': [{
                    'type': 'paragraph',
                    'content': content_text,
                    'inline': [{'type': 'text', 'value': content_text}]
                }]
            })
            continue
        # paragraph
        para_lines=[]
        while i < len(lines) and lines[i].strip():
            # break if special
            if lines[i].strip().startswith("```"):
                break
            if '|' in lines[i] and i+1 < len(lines) and re.match(r'^\s*\|?[\s\-\|:]+\|?', lines[i+1]) and '|' in lines[i+1]:
                break
            if re.match(r'^\s*([-*+]\s+|\d+\.\s+)', lines[i]):
                break
            if lines[i].lstrip().startswith('>'):
                break
            para_lines.append(lines[i])
            i+=1
            if i < len(lines) and not lines[i].strip():
                break
        para_text=" ".join([l.strip() for l in para_lines])
        # inline parse
        def parse_inline(s):
            res=[]
            pattern=re.compile(r'(\*\*(.+?)\*\*|!\[([^\]]*)\]\(([^\)]+)\)|\[([^\]]+)\]\(([^\)]+)\))')
            pos=0
            for mm in pattern.finditer(s):
                start,end=mm.span()
                if start>pos:
                    res.append({'type':'text','value':s[pos:start]})
                if mm.group(2):
                    res.append({'type':'strong','value':mm.group(2)})
                elif mm.group(3) is not None:
                    alt=mm.group(3)
                    src_full=mm.group(4)
                    src=src_full.split()[0]
                    title=None
                    tm=re.search(r'["\'](.+)["\']', src_full)
                    if tm:
                        title=tm.group(1)
                    res.append({'type':'image','alt':alt,'src':src,'title':title})
                elif mm.group(5) is not None:
                    t=mm.group(5)
                    url_full=mm.group(6)
                    url=url_full.split()[0]
                    title=None
                    tm=re.search(r'["\'](.+)["\']', url_full)
                    if tm:
                        title=tm.group(1)
                    res.append({'type':'link','text':t,'url':url,'title':title})
                pos=end
            if pos < len(s):
                res.append({'type':'text','value':s[pos:]})
            if not res:
                res.append({'type':'text','value':s})
            return res
        inlines=parse_inline(para_text)
        blocks.append({
            'type':'paragraph',
            'content':para_text,
            'inline':inlines
        })
    return blocks

# Ensure compile.sh works on fresh checkout: it currently does tail -n +2 treemd.py >> executable
# That works if treemd.py exists (which now is committed)

rm executable
./compile.sh
./executable --version
./executable -l /tmp/test.md
./executable --tree /tmp/test.md
./executable --count /tmp/test.md
echo "---test compile fresh---"
# Simulate fresh checkout by removing executable and also __pycache__
rm -rf __pycache__ executable
./compile.sh && echo "compile ok" && ./executable --version && ./executable -l /tmp/test.md | head

# Check git status: executable should be ignored (untracked but ignored)
git status --porcelain
git status --ignored | head -n 20
